title: Project Business Context
description: Per-project business context. Stored at projects/{slug}/business-context.json. Read by every skill to inherit voice, audience, location, YMYL, publish policy. Schema added 2026-05-22 (v5.0 Stage B) — was referenced by projects but never validated. Strictness is intentionally lenient on existing fields to avoid breaking legacy projects; new fields under `location.*` formalize the 5-archetype + 3-tier schema-mapping model from references/local/industry-to-schema-mapping.md.

site_slug.description: Lowercase kebab-case. Matches projects/{slug}/ directory name.

location.description: Geographic + business-archetype context. v5.0 Stage B added the business_archetype + business_category + schema_org_type + local_article_pattern fields, which drive schema-generator's auto-selection. See references/local/industry-to-schema-mapping.md for the canonical model.

business_archetype.description: v5.0 Stage B. A=local brick-and-mortar; B=service-area business; C=multi-location chain; D=national ecommerce; E=pure SaaS / online service. Determines schema shape (LocalBusiness vs Organization, single vs chain, areaServed vs spatialCoverage). See references/local/industry-to-schema-mapping.md §1.

business_category.description: v5.0 Stage B. Free-text industry slug. Tier 1 closed-enum values (e.g. 'plumber', 'dentist', 'restaurant') resolve deterministically. Tier 2 values trigger a soft warning. Tier 3 (anything else) requires manual schema_org_type override. See industry-to-schema-mapping.md §2.

schema_org_type.description: v5.0 Stage B. The Schema.org @type leaf the publisher's schema-generator emits (e.g. 'Dentist', 'OnlineStore', 'LegalService', 'Organization'). Auto-filled by Tier 1/2 resolution; required manually for Tier 3. Wins over archetype default when present.

additional_type.description: v5.0 Stage B. Optional. Schema.org additionalType (URL or ProductOntology) for industries without a native Schema.org leaf. Example: 'https://www.productontology.org/id/Horticultural_lighting' for cannabis B2B equipment.

local_article_pattern.description: v5.0 Stage B. Schema pattern for '[keyword] [location]' articles. service_area = Service.areaServed (true geographic service; archetype A/B/C default). spatial_coverage = Article.spatialCoverage + about + mentions (Wirecutter pattern; archetype D/E default — writing ABOUT a place vs serving it). See industry-to-schema-mapping.md §4.

ymyl_flag.description: v5.0 Stage B. True if business is YMYL (medical, legal, financial, news-current-events). Triggers additional Schema.org credentials + lastReviewed + Person.hasCredential emissions.

service_areas.description: v5.0 Stage B. Geographic scope of business operations.

nap.description: v5.0 Stage B. Name + Address + Phone for LocalBusiness schema. Optional — when absent, the schema-generator falls back to opportunistic mode (omits LocalBusiness emission). NEVER fabricate.

gbp.description: v5.0 Stage B. Google Business Profile reference. Optional — when present, becomes sameAs link in schema.

shipping.description: v5.0 Stage B. Ecommerce / physical-goods shipping context. Drives Product.offers.shippingDetails.

local_seo_mode.description: v5.0 Stage B. off = no local SEO routing even on keyword+location queries. opportunistic = route to local-* template when geo modifier detected (default for projects with full location.*). primary_strategy = aggressive local content (multi-state pillars + city pages by default).

local_authority_links_by_state.description: v5.0 Stage B. Per-state map of authoritative outbound link URLs (trade associations, regulators, press). Used by writer agents for credible local-content outbound linking.

pair.description: Voice register pair. Accepts EITHER a 2-element array ["warm", "technical"] OR a single slash-joined string "warm / technical". scripts/validate/title_validator.infer_register() reads both shapes (isinstance list/str) and several projects (project-juliet/project-kilo/project-hotel) legitimately use the string form, so both are valid (schema loosened 2026-07-09, v3.38 Task 7 — was array-only, which failed those three projects on a field the code already handled).

citation_source_policy.description: Competitor/peer-domain citation guard (added 2026-06-20). When present and enabled, competitor websites are excluded from in-text citations, the References list, body outbound links, and JSON-LD citation/sameAs. Enforced by scripts/_core/competitor_domains.py across the whole pipeline. Absent or exclude_competitor_domains=false or enforcement=off → fully disabled (backward compatible). See root CLAUDE.md Rule 8 + docs/superpowers/specs/2026-06-20-competitor-citation-exclusion-design.md.

cta.description: Designed CTA module config (v3.34, 2026-07-04). Consumed by scripts/optimize/cta_injector.py (mandatory 'cta-injection' stage): injects '### {heading}' + one variant paragraph as a styled .xr-cta-box conversion card. Absent or enabled=false → full no-op (backward compatible). The heading MUST be classifiable by scripts/_core/component_headings COMPONENTS['cta'] or the publisher will never tag it. Verified live by verify_post check 29.

placements.description: mid = after the content section at the ~35% word mark; end = before Further Reading/References (BOFU slot). DEFAULT (v3.41.5, operator decision 2026-07-24): ["mid"] — the product grid + CTA belong in the article's front-middle, not the end. 'end' remains a legal value for backward compatibility but NO project or format uses it: the last exception (weekly-digest) was retired 2026-07-25. tests/test_cta_placement_mid_default_seam.py pins the code default, every project config, and the no-end rule.

format_rules.description: v3.35.1: per-format placement override — {format_id: [placements]}. Formats not listed use the global placements. Since 2026-07-25 NO rule may carry "end" (the weekly-digest end exception was retired; the fleet test enforces this) — use this only to NARROW to ["mid"] or to disable a format via [].

variants.description: Per-placement copy variants; the injector rotates deterministically by task_id. Each text = ONE markdown paragraph with ≥1 markdown link. No em-dashes (sanitized to commas), no UTM on internal links (GA4 self-referral).

conversion_offers.description: Business-model-aware conversion-offer catalog consumed by scripts/optimize/cta_brief_builder.py (Step 1 of the cta-writer pipeline). Absent = old static cta.variants path runs unchanged.

services.description: b2b_services only. One entry per service page.

category_routing_map.description: b2b_services only. Path to the project's machine-readable blog-category -> service lookup JSON.

catalog_path.description: ecommerce only (v3.38). Optional override for the product-catalog.json path read by cta_brief_builder.py's ecommerce resolver. Plugin-root-relative or absolute. Defaults to projects/{slug}/product-catalog.json.

default_category.description: ecommerce only (v3.38). Product-category slug (or human name) used as the fallback when no SKU or category token-match resolves. Must exist in the synced catalog with count>0 to be used, else the brief degrades to a link-only (no-shortcode) shop CTA.

fallback_url.description: ecommerce only (v3.38). Shop/collection URL used as the brief's target_url (WooCommerce category permalinks are not present in the cached catalog). Null target_url is tolerated by verify_post check 29 because the shortcode, not the link, is the conversion element.

constraints.description: Per-project cta-writer/tone constraints, copied verbatim into cta-brief.json and read by the cta-writer dispatch + tone gate. Known keys below; any additional keys pass through.

company.description: Company identity and team/proof-points for byline authority signals.

host_access.description: Shell access to the WordPress FILESYSTEM, for hop 2->3 artifacts that are files on the host rather than REST resources (currently the blog-sidebars mu-plugin). Without it scripts.wordpress.deploy_blog_sidebars reports 'manual' with exact steps rather than guessing at a transport — it never silently skips. Contains no credentials: `ssh` is an ssh-config host alias, so the key stays in the ssh agent.

mu_plugins.description: absolute mu-plugins path in the container

blog_sidebars.description: Blog sidebar config (v3.42.4). Consumed by scripts/build/blog_sidebar_generator.py, which renders projects/{slug}/brand/blog-sidebars.php (an mu-plugin registering two widget areas) + blog-sidebars.css. Two DIFFERENT sidebars by design: the blog index helps a reader FIND (its own Categories widget first), the single post PROMOTES (image-led CTA card, products, other pages). Absent or enabled=false -> nothing is generated and the theme's existing sidebar is untouched. The generator never edits the theme's shared widget area.

class_prefix.description: CSS/PHP namespace. MUST be added to any Remove-Unused-CSS safelist (FlyingPress/Perfmatters/LiteSpeed) or the stylesheet is stripped in production while looking fine to a logged-in admin.

index_modules.description: Order top-to-bottom on the blog index. Default ['categories','cta_card','products','page_promo'].

post_modules.description: Order top-to-bottom on a single post. Default ['cta_card','products','page_promo'] — promotional, no navigation.

product_category.description: Product category slug for the promo module. Falls back to conversion_offers.default_category.

excluded_product_categories.description: Never merchandised from editorial content. MERGED with conversion_offers.excluded_categories and hard-blocked in the widget, so a sidebar cannot become a second route to a regulated/prescription line.

promo_pages.description: Pages the page-promo module pushes when there is nothing contextual (on an article it prefers sibling guides). Derived from anchor_links when omitted.

cta_post.description: CTA card on articles: {kicker,title,btn,url,img}. img is a WP attachment ID. A card missing url or title renders nothing.

cta_index.description: CTA card on the blog index. Same shape as cta_post.

palette.description: Optional colour overrides (primary/accent/accent_dark/surface/surface_2/ink/muted). Otherwise resolved from brand-identity brand_visuals, then brand-config colors.
